name: AI Chat Area
tagline: An Android app that puts a chat interface in front of hosted large language models.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a chat UI wired to somebody else's model API, which is the single most cloned piece of software of the last few years. Streaming responses, a message list, conversation history, a system prompt box: an agent will produce all of it in an afternoon, and the actual intelligence comes from the same upstream models either way. The only real difference is that you supply your own API key and pay per token instead of paying a monthly fee to a store listing. If your usage is light, that swap is usually cheaper; if you send novels every day, metered billing can bite. Build it as an installable PWA and you get something you can open from your phone home screen without ever touching an app store.
coreLoopDIY: A local, installable chat app that streams answers from an OpenAI-compatible API, saves conversations on-device, and lets you switch models and system prompts.
requirements: An API key for an OpenAI-compatible provider (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, or a local Ollama endpoint)
Node 20 and a browser; a static host or your own laptop for serving the PWA
Willingness to pay per token instead of per month
whatYouLose: A real Play Store install with updates, permissions, and offline packaging handled for you
Someone else eating the API bill and hiding key management from you
Whatever preset personas, prompt packs, or extras the app bundles
Native Android niceties: share sheet targets, notifications, background behavior
Cross-device history sync, unless you build a backend you then have to maintain
moatNotes: The models are rented, not owned. What is left is app store distribution and a UI that does not feel like a weekend project.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most people paying for an app like this are not paying for technology, they are paying to not think about API keys, token pricing, or which model is currently good. A flat fee on a store listing is legible; a metered bill from a provider dashboard is not. There is also the install path: tapping a green button is a different experience from cloning a repo and deploying a PWA, and for a lot of users that gap never closes no matter how simple the code is.
notes: The hard part of an AI chat app is being the model, and nobody here is the model.
prompt:
Build a personal AI chat app as an installable PWA. Empty folder, no scaffolding questions, just pick and go.

Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, Dexie (IndexedDB) for storage, vite-plugin-pwa for the manifest and service worker. No backend, no accounts, no analytics.

Core behavior:
- Sidebar with a list of conversations: create, rename, delete, plus a search box that filters on message text.
- Main pane: message thread with user and assistant bubbles, markdown rendering, fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting and a copy button.
- Composer: textarea, Enter to send, Shift+Enter for newline, a stop button that aborts the in-flight request.
- Stream responses token by token from an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint using fetch with ReadableStream parsing of SSE lines. Handle abort cleanly and persist partial output.
- Per-conversation settings drawer: model name, system prompt, temperature. Defaults come from a global settings page.
- Settings page: base URL, API key, default model, default system prompt. Store base URL and model in localStorage.
- Key handling: read VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY and VITE_OPENAI_BASE_URL from .env for local dev, and allow overriding the key in Settings where it is kept in localStorage only. Write .env.example, gitignore .env, and say plainly in the README that a browser-held key is fine for a personal app and not fine for anything shared.
- Reusable system prompts: a small named-preset list the user can save and apply to new conversations.
- Export a conversation as markdown, and export all data as one JSON file with an import button.
- Mobile first layout: sidebar collapses to a drawer under 768px, safe-area padding, PWA manifest with icons so it installs to a phone home screen.

Out of scope: user auth, multi-device sync, image generation, file uploads, voice, RAG, billing, telemetry.

Deliver a README with setup, a dev command, a build command, and one paragraph on cost: this bills per token through the provider, so a heavy day costs more than a light month.
